summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, and a history of anticoagulation was admitted after developing sudden palpitations during dialysis. Initial evaluation ruled out pulmonary embolism, pneumonia, and pericardial effusion. She was diagnosed with supraventricular tachycardia, which resolved with adenosine and was managed with metoprolol after ablation was deferred due to complex vascular anatomy in the groin. During admission, she developed multiple MRSA abscesses requiring incision and drainage; antibiotic therapy was optimized with increased Bactrim dosing after poor response. Chronic bilateral DVTs and a right femoral arteriovenous fistula or malformation were identified on imaging. Her warfarin dose was adjusted due to interactions with rifampin, and she remained stable on dialysis. She was discharged to extended care with medication changes, including higher-dose Bactrim, continued metoprolol, and 9 mg warfarin daily, with close follow-up planned for INR monitoring, abscess healing, and vascular evaluation.
